blockers.description: A same-day drop-in pass can be held but never paid for. confirmBooking (src/app/actions/booking.ts:723) refuses when bk.startsAt <= now, but a drop-in booking's starts_at is the venue's OPENING instant. createOpenCapacityHold deliberately moved its expiry cap to ends_at for exactly this reason (src/lib/availability/units.ts:731) and read-model.ts:369 makes a date bookable until CLOSING. Buy a pass after opening time -> hold mints, reserve page renders, Confirm & pay returns 'expired'.
blockers.workaround: none — blocks the ordinary purchase path

blockers.description: Editing operating hours re-keys the admissions counter. The advisory lock is hashtextextended(listing_id || ':' || openIso), derived from the opening instant; src/app/actions/operating-hours.ts (100 lines) has zero booking/occupancy/mode-lock awareness. Shift opening 06:00 -> 07:00 and taken reads 0, so a second full cap becomes sellable for the same date — an overbook path around the guarantee the phase exists to provide.

Host 'Blocked dates' do nothing on a drop-in listing. availability_block is read once in read-model.ts:220-224, BELOW the open fork at :196; getOpenDay, the month query and the claim never read it, while the host page still renders BlocksEditor and 09-UI-SPEC 1g promises blocks zero a date.

A listing can publish in drop-in mode with a NULL per-person price (wizard orders occupancy before pricing; saveListingStep never re-runs publishSchema on an already-published row). The booker's click reaches quoteOpenCapacity(null), which throws -> mapBookingError re-throws -> raw 500 on the money path (the T-03-500 outcome its own docblock forbids).

createGroup has no occupancy-mode check. Four files hard-code openCapacity: false relying on a UI-only condition whose comment claims a server-side re-check that does not exist. One paid pass => capacity_snapshot = max_occupancy - 1 (the DAILY cap) and invite emails describing a 16-hour reservation.

A booker cannot buy a second set of passes for a date they already hold. findOwnOpenHold matches status='confirmed' AND starts_at = <the whole date>, so the D-42 replay swallows the purchase and silently redirects to the existing booking — while PASSES_FIXED_MESSAGE tells the booker to book them separately.

context_notes: The phase's new mechanism held up under adversarial review — the advisory lock is genuinely the first statement, the sweep/SUM/INSERT sit inside it, openTakenSql is really shared between claim and read model, both mutations refuse the other occupancy mode from the persisted row, and host-cancel correctly skips the availability_block. Every defect found is at a SEAM: date-shaped bookings meeting window-shaped machinery inherited from the exclusive path. That is the frame to carry into gap closure — do not go looking for flaws in the claim itself, look at every place a drop-in booking is handed to code written for an hours-and-minutes reservation.
